[TAB]Amathaon is known to bless whomever he will, without regard to how they use their talents for good or evil. He answers no prayers and has no priests, but there is a thriving cult of patrons that honor him by supporting the gifted. Most only recognize talents that have been honed for years, and seek to house only masterpieces in their galleries. [PARAGRAPH:1]The most devout know better. Masterworks never come from pure inspiration, but from grueling labor that honors Kilmorph, Cernunnos, Sucellus, or Nantosuelta more than Amathaon by the time they are complete. The God of Creation is best served by encouraging the raw talents of the young. [PARAGRAPH:1]The strangest Museum in Erebus celebrates failure as much as success. It houses more than its share of great works in every medium, but most are either unfinished or ruined. The sketches of toddlers adorn the same walls and are shown equal honor. [PARAGRAPH:1]Children are always welcome to wander its corridors, to climb or juggle ancient sculptures, to draw over oil paintings, and to generally enjoy themselves learning without a fear of punishment. Most see their behavior as wasteful and destructive, which it certainly is, but the curators know the value that can emerge from creative chaos. [PARAGRAPH:1]There is no set curriculum for pupils at the Museum, but masters are invited from far and wide to tutor them on any subject they request. Most masters leave having learned more than they taught. Many swear that their young charges could not be mere mortals, but must be pixies or even the Archangel Maponos in disguise.

The Crucible could spell the end of all spells, and mean the death of the Age of Rebirth. It refines the world of Erebus, purifying it of the taints of both hell and sorcery. So long as it remains active it will continue to reduce the Armageddon Counter while depleting all the mana in the world, until not even the greatest archmage can accomplish what once came easily to any adept. Anyone who depends on magic is advised to raze this wonder to the ground as soon as possible. [PARAGRAPH:3][H1]Background:[\\H1]"Embarr was reborn at the end of the Age of Rebirth, at the dawn of the Age of Invention. After the Fane of Lessers had been conquered and Basium marched his Mercurian army into hell to confront the demons directly. Within Judicium the Bannor forged the Crucible, which began drawing off the magic of the world and making spells more and more difficult to cast and man began to rely more on science. This is when Embarr's scattered pieces were brought back together, to bring the world steam power, medicine and astronomy. "[PARAGRAPH:2]"It works on the principle that there is a finite amount of magic in the word. So Bannor enchanters created a version of the immovable object (the crucible) and an unstoppable force (a great ball that rolls inside it, ever trying to go forward only to grind against the walls of the crucible). The Bannor believe that the word is better without magic, which is why they try to draw it off. They stop the crucible once per year to allow them to charge their magical items (they don't want the world to have magic but they allow their most trusted to carry very powerful artifacts). A few generations into the age of invention most don't believe in magic, but these Bannor witch hunters scour the land looking for demons and places of lingering power. "--Kael, on Reddit

Late in the Age of Rebirth, after the Illians are defeated on the Aquilo Tundra, Falamar and Rhoanna settle as rulers on a chain of islands in the Meditor sea. They choose the islands for their beauty, but also because it allows them to maintain a vigil on both the nearby Deadlands and the Fane of Lessers. [PARAGRAPH]They name their new city the Bay of Laurus and it quickly grows to a major port for the region and an example of freedom and tolerance that hasn't been seen since the early days of the Patrian Empire. It is where the Children of Cliodna found their first temple to the Matronae. [PARAGRAPH]The Nether Blade is stored in the Bay of Laurus and Os-Gabella ends up traveling to the city to attempt to find it and use it to end her immortal life. Before she does so she discovers the Jeteye dealers of the cities ports and finds some measure of escape in the delusions and opiate dreams the drug offers. Somewhere among the cities beggars the first human lives in squalor, once queen of the Sheaim, once grandmother to the Calabim, once unwilling bride to the god Nemed, her world is now little more than visions and dancing shadows. More than one man seeking to abuse or hurt the cities beggars has met his end when he assumed Os-Gabella was just another broken vagrant. [PARAGRAPH]But the Heron Throne is the story you asked for. And it is a modest one. The Heron Throne is actually not magical at all. It is the throne Falamar and Rhoanna share. Their rule is fair and respected among their people and from other empires who sail to the island to receive their council. [PARAGRAPH]The physical Heron Throne is an artistic masterpiece crafted of beautiful white marble during the Age of Magic. It was from this throne that Soqed Hozi oversaw the administration of the complex laws of Patria. The term "Heron Throne" itself is most often a metonymy for her administration, as "The Crown" is for the state run in the name of many monarchs. The Heron Throne was a core part of the Patrian government, responsible for protecting the empire from internal threats, and enforcing the ever increasing laws. Chief among their roles was the tight control of magic and rituals, that it would never slip away from the control of the members of the Imprimatur Council. [PARAGRAPH]SOQED was Member of the Imprimatur Council, the greatest master of Law Magic the word has ever known, and the Matriarch of the Order during the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH]It is said that if Soqed spoke a lie, reality would change to make it into truth. Soqed had a mute twin who was little more than a dim shadow of her powerful sister. The two remained at the Temple of Atonement where they oversaw the church and its inquisitors. [PARAGRAPH]Unknown to even Soqed, their father was a Historian, a True Angel of Oghma. The angel fell in love with Soqed's mother, spent 21 days with her and then used his power to unwrite his time with her so that no one in creation would remember it. But he did allow her to keep the twin daughters he had impregnated her with. [PARAGRAPH]During the Third Rebellion, Soqed's sister was sending messages to Kylorin and the Sanctus Inquisition, telling them what she knew about the plans of the Heron Throne. When Soqed found out she murdered her sister, beating her with a ceremonial mace in the Temple of Atonement's large kitchen. At the moment of her sister's death Soqed lost both her affinity for Law magic and her ability to speak. When the guards came to investigate the sound of the fight they incorrectly assumed that Soqed was her mute sister, and the dead body on the floor was Soqed. Nothing Soqed could do would convince them, and they tried and executed her for her own murder. [PARAGRAPH]The Heron Throne founded the Order not from divine inspiration but from the growing requirements of the Patrian bureaucracy. The codex of Patrian law had become so byzantine and severe that nearly autonomous inquisitors were needed to carry out it requirements. These inquisitors were magically bound to the codex so that they wouldn't become corrupted by their station. They drew upon the name of Junil, god of Law, in taking their oaths and in carrying out their brutal decrees. [PARAGRAPH]These inquisitors were feared nearly as much as Kylorin's Archmages and would come to a city to adjudicate major disputes and to see that justice, as defined by the codex of Patria, was followed. Some inquisitors began to question why Patrian law superseded the worship of Junil and when the Heron Throne found out that these concerns were growing they launched the Purge of Whispers, the execution of anyone the Throne suspected of having these views. It all happened in one night, and it effectively ended any unrest and solidified the Heron Thrones hold on the Church during the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH]Today's Order is not proud of their history and would prefer to bury it. Some say they gave away the Throne not out of any love for Falamar or Rhoanna's reign, but because they would rather eliminate any reminders of their less that righteous origins.

Late in the Age of Rebirth, after the destruction of the Throne of Hell, a great prison is built by the Bannor in the Fane of Lessers. This prison is made to imprison demons by using enchantments gained by the study of Basium's cudgel. The guard have little to do with men, and don't believe in killing demons, which only returns them to hell. Instead they trap them and bring them to be held eternally within Judicium. --Kael, on Reddit

[ICON_BULLET]The [LINK=BUILDING_LORUM_DIABOLI]Lorum Diaboli[\\LINK] wonder imprisons demons, so they they cannot return to plague Erebus again. Its construction lowers the Armageddon Counter, but its main effect it that it grants [LINK=PROMOTION_CUSTOS_JUDICII]Judicium Guard[\\LINK] promotion to units in its city. In addition to serving as an inverse of the [LINK=PROMOTION_PROPHECY_MARK]Prophecy Mark[\\LINK] promotion, reducing the AC for each unit built, it captures demons in the same way as Basium's [LINK=PROMOTION_ANGELORUM_CAVEA]Angelorum Cavea[\\LINK]. (Unlike that weapon, it lets evil mortal souls go free, but it still prevents demons from enjoying immortality. ) Razing the city containing the wonder may free all of the demons imprisoned there, just like [LINK=SPELL_DESTROY_ANGELORUM_CAVEA]destroying the Angelorum Cavea[\\LINK] does.

Every Throne could be considered its own sect. There is no common communication, rules or traditions between them. Some are brutal and vengeful, others are lighthearted and free. They tend to be the opposite of the communities they exist in. Sometimes they are the secret power behind the city government, and sometimes they are teenage adventurers pretending at being a secret organization.

The Slyph Search wonder may found the Foxmen religion, provide Air mana, make units Light, and help generate Drifters, but it will not stay in one place for very long. There is nothing permanent except change, especially when it comes to Tali. The center of his worship moves itself often and without warning. It prefers to visit cities with more air mana and less earth mana, or where the Foxmen faith already has a presence, but can go anywhere. That includes cities belonging to your rivals.
